Title: Mapping codes to LOINC with or without SNOMED - General - LOINC Community Forum
# Mapping codes to LOINC with or without SNOMED. I am seeking advice on the best approach to map local microbiology examinations codes to LOINC codes. The team I’m working with proposed two potential approaches. For example, in the case of describing a “Body fluid culture result,” the options are:. 1.Use the most specific LOINC code : For example, LOINC 6114-6 | Bacteria identified in Body fluid by culture. 2.Use a general LOINC code combined with a SNOMED code : For example, LOINC 6463-4 | Bacteria identified in Specimen by Culture, combined with SNOMED code 258450006 | Cerebrospinal fluid specimen (specimen). Which approach would be recommended un this case? I’ll tell you my usual strategy:. If your LIS has specific fields for specimens (as is often the case these days), these fields should be mapped to SNOMED codes within the specimen hierarchy. SNOMED provides a more complex ontology than what is typically required in microbiology. In the procedures field, we use LOINC codes. The difference between specimen-specific codes and specimen-agnostic codes is defined by the clinical or process relevance of the specimen. Is your procedure validated for a limited list of specific specimens? Is your post-analytical process dependent on the type of specimen used? If so, use specimen-specific codes. If not, use general codes “in specimen” and rely on the specific field for specimen identification. Hi Ella, Ivan stated it very well. I would like to add a note about using the SNOMED code for Specimen. This is in relation to the LOINC SNOMED collaborative work. Specimen that are mapped to a SNOMED codes will have a one to one mapping to a LOINC codes going forward(maybe not right now, but this is the strategy for the close future). I reiterate from Ivan that it depends on your ultimate use case in analytics, and reporting that will justify what you are going to map to currently. Thank you Ivan , and Ella if you have further questions, please let us know or If you need a concept that is not in the DB, please submit. Powered by Discourse, best viewed with JavaScript enabled.

results.content: # Culture Tests - Order Codes. **Culture Test Order Codes…** In our LIS we have different culture tests based on the type of specimen. Option 1 : -Map the order tests to respective ‘Bacteria identified’ codes in LOINC. Option 2 : All the routine culture will be ordered as a 6463-4 (Bacteria identified in Unspecified specimen by Culture) and the specimen type will not be part of the code ( will be mentioned separately in HL7 OBR). As we need to mention specimen/site type separately in HL7 message, is there any other issue in mapping all Routine Culture tests to a single LOINC? Is this the way culture orders should be mapped? Hello and thank you for asking about microbiology culture tests. One situation to ascertain beforehand is that the routine blood culture does only identify bacteria, in order to use the “Bacteria Identified” series of LOINC codes. If the cultures will also identify fungi, viruses, or non-bacteria, there is LOINC code 11475-1 Microorganism identified:Prid:Pt:XXX:Nom:Culture and. Where there is not an appropriate LOINC code for the specimen source from your listing, post the individual display names here, and we’ll try to help you before determining if it’s necessary to submit a new request to Regenstrief. If our clients’ systems use only one code for cultures, one code for stains, etc, we will use option #2 to map to LOINC. Thank you Ms. Pam Banning for the information on Culture Test mapping. I also would like to know how Histopathology Tests are mapped in LOINC. Following are few culture tests that we could not map to LOINC. EYE SWAB CULTURE (Similar to 609-8 (Bacteria identified in Eye by Aerobe culture) but method as ‘Culture’). There are few Microscopy tests also that we could not map. results.title: Mapping between order codes and loinc result codes - General - LOINC Community Forum
results.content: Is there a mapping available that links order codes to LOINC result codes? If you are asking about test order codes (and not LOINC codes) that each performing laboratory may use as a unique identifier to the test order on their menu, a number of reference labs will provide some of the information in their test compendium (or CLIA Specimen Collection Manual in the US). Along with the test information, many labs are providing which results are part of order panels, as well as the LOINC codes for each result. You’ll see the LOINC order code first, followed by the result items that are part of their CBC and their LOINCs. Are you also asking about non panel order LOINC codes such as when there is a single orderable, which is also a single resultable? If so there are LOINC codes with a OrdObs indication of Both, indicating the same LOINC code can be used for when the lab test is an order and also when it is a result.

Certara 为生物技术、制药和 CRO 量身定制解决方案，应对独特挑战，推动成功。. Home / Blog / **Why Should You Use LOINC Codes For SDTM?**. # Why Should You Use LOINC Codes For SDTM? In this blog, we take a detailed look at LOINC Codes and SDTM. We look at several LOINC code examples and examine why it’s beneficial to use the codes alongside CDISC and NCI controlled terminology. We also include details of where to find the official LOINC codes list. ## What Are LOINC Codes Used For? Essentially, LOINC provides a unique identifier for each medical observation – such as lab test. It also provides additional information, such as standardized specimen type, category, etc. It is often requested in regulatory data submissions to provide context to clinical measurement data, for example, Labs and ECG (electrocardiogram). ## Important Information About LOINC Codes For SDTM. CDISC and the NCI provide controlled terms for observations such as Lab test names, for example LBTESTCD (Laboratory Test Code) and LBTEST (the name of the lab test performed). The CDISC/NCI controlled terms for Lab test are not unique. But LOINC codes are unique, so only the LOINC code is required to identify the test. From the CDISC NCI SDTM Controlled terms:. However, this is simply “A measurement of the glucose in a biological specimen.”Therefore the “specimen” is required to identify the measurement. CDISC NCI SDTM also provides a list of terms for Specimen (see below):. CDISC NCI SDTM also provides controlled terms for the different types of measurement e.g. Test strip (dipstick) vs. To represent a lab test in SDTM, several columns (LBTESTCD, LBSPEC, LBMETHOD etc.) are required, each having a different set of controlled terms. However, LOINC provides a unique “code” for each test, along with an SDTM mapping to specimen type, method, units, etc. Below is a breakdown of the LOINC codes for the Glucose example:.
